conditions.text: All pronghorn hunting in Idaho is by controlled hunt: a controlled hunt tag for this hunt number, with a hunting license, is required. North Ground cannot see whether you were drawn or hold one.
Any person hunting in an archery only season, including controlled hunts, must have their license with archery permit validation.
Any person hunting in a muzzleloader only season, including controlled hunts, must have their license with muzzleloader permit validation.
Youth only hunt; see pages 110 and 114 of the booklet for who qualifies.
A hunter report is due within 10 days after harvest, or within 10 days after the season closes if you do not harvest.

limitations: Idaho also issues 5 Landowner Permission Hunts for doe or fawn pronghorn (Unit 63; Portion of Units 54, 55 and 57; Portion of units 43, 44 and 45; Private land in Units 46, 47, 54, 55, 56 and 57; Units 52 and 45), published in a separate brochure. North Ground has not certified them; if your tag is for one, this answer does not describe it.
Idaho's unit map is a best representation; the written unit and hunt area descriptions in the booklet control. Near a boundary, confirm which unit you are in.
Motorized-vehicle rules, federal land rules (including Idaho National Laboratory and Craters of the Moon), wildlife management area restrictions and landowner permission are not evaluated.
This is a state-licensed recreational result. It does not describe hunting under tribal authority or treaty rights, which North Ground does not evaluate.

drawCycles.name: 2026 controlled hunt drawing (deer, elk, pronghorn)
drawCycles.statedAs: Dates to Remember (p. 7): first application period May 1 – June 5, results posted by early July; second application period August 5 – 15, notified by August 25; leftover tags on sale August 25 at 10 a.m. Mountain Time.
